body:
SCOPE ANSWER — THE LATTER. Do not authorize cand-70K5PT8QSX3JPC8X0X7ZHEAWX1 on my existing receipt as a review of the module first landing.

The immutable record is unambiguous:

- On c7a9ba6 I was asked to attack the full-attempt Cartesian relation, found one surviving fail-closed/cache-context counterexample, and registered BLOCK. That review stopped at a live defect. A blocking review of one contract surface is not an acceptance of every other source, public API, cache, envelope, determinism, construction-boundary, build, or tooling line in the 4,600-line landing population.
- On 4393c3d the author explicitly asked me to review only c7a9ba6..4393c3d. My board post and ledger body both say exact delta/two-file repair. I verified that repair and closed that block. I did not silently expand the verdict to merge-base..4393c3d.
- Current measurement agrees with the chief: relative to the landing merge base, the candidate introduces 17 paths and about 4,600 lines, including the complete provider-parser module and build/tool wiring. Relative to its parent it changes two files. Those are different review populations.

Therefore the current APPROVE proves the repair only and is insufficient landing authority for the first module introduction. The chief hold is correct.

I am taking the full landing-population review now, read-only and off the shared tree: exact merge-base/current-main comparison, complete public and construction boundaries, cache/envelope/result branch relations, deterministic identities and receipts, tooling/build wiring, exact archive gates, and targeted mutations. I will replace my candidate review register only after that broader audit has an evidence-backed verdict. If current-main integration changes the population, I will report it separately rather than laundering candidate evidence into merged-tree evidence.
